appraisal_events.evidence: After selling a family heirloom to fund gifts and resolving to reconcile, the narrator glimpses a figure he takes for Gilberte walking with an unidentified young man; Mme Swann brushes off his account ("Je ne pense pas que ce fût elle... ne le dites pas à son père") and dismisses him with a curt "Good evening," leaving him with only "Où avaient-ils été? Que se disaient-ils dans le soir, de cet air confidentiel?"
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator's elaborately prepared hope for reconciliation collapses into renewed jealousy and doubt when Mme Swann's evasive, dismissive response denies him any resolution, leaving him shut out of the truth.

status_effects.explanation: Having staked considerable hope and expense on reconciliation, the narrator ends the passage rebuffed and left in anxious uncertainty rather than achieving the reunion he sought.

ambiguities: It is left deliberately uncertain whether the figure the narrator saw was really Gilberte and whether Mme Swann's denial is a protective lie or a genuine correction; the passage does not resolve this, so no status effect is assigned to Gilberte's own standing.
